rationale: This is a tiny (2903 text bytes, 7 functions, dominated by main/mkmatrix/mmult) Shootout matrix benchmark whose interesting logic sits in tight integer loops (mmult triple loop, matrix init/free), so the controlling concern is protecting a very small hot region without inflating a 3 KB binary or slowing the loops: control-flow bloat passes get the highest cost weights (FLA RuntimeCost/SizeCost 0.85/0.8, BCF 0.75/0.8) so they are applied sparingly — ideally only to cold wrapper functions like main's setup/teardown paths — while SUB gets a low RuntimeCost/SizeCost (0.25/0.2) and high SecurityGain (0.7) because instruction substitution obscures the arithmetic of mmult at near-zero overhead and is essentially always safe; ICALL is favored (SecurityGain 0.65, moderate costs) since indirect-calling mkmatrix/mmult/zeromatrix hides the small program's very static call graph, and IBR (0.6 security) cheaply breaks basic-block contiguity inside main without the blowup of FLA; SPLIT is kept moderate (0.45/0.5) because the functions are already tiny and splitting yields limited gain but costs little; IGV gets mid-range weights — useful for flattening the visible data-flow of the mmult loop but with genuine runtime and correctness exposure in tightly-scheduled loops. All correctness risks are kept low-to-moderate given the code is straight-line numeric C++ with no exception-heavy or complex control-flow constructs that would make any pass hazardous.
